To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The double-differential cross section d2σ/dpdt for charged pion production in proton–tungsten interactions has been measured in the momentum range 0.1 GeV/c ≤p<0.8 GeV/c, and in the transverse momentum range 0 ≤|pT|<0.4 GeV/c.

we have measured the double-differential pion cross-section for protons on tantalum at four incident momenta in a large range of angles and momenta, and that we have measured pion yields for typical neutrino factory design parameters.

the pion yield in a typical neutrino factory beamline is 1–2 orders of magnitude higher than the pion yield predicted by the FLUKA Monte Carlo simulation, that the yield of positive pions is about 1.3 times higher than that of negative pions, and that the yield of pions is almost independent of the proton beam momentum in the range from 5 GeV/c to 12 GeV/c.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of charged mesons in the forward region in proton–nucleus collisions at intermediate energies.
the production of charged particles by protons on nuclear targets at beam momenta in the range of 1 to 12 GeV/c, and with the subsequent transport of these particles through matter.
the production of charged particles in the interaction of high-energy protons with nuclear targets, in particular the production of pions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data presented in this paper are of high quality and are well described by the Monte Carlo generator used in the analysis.
the present results are in good agreement with existing data.

the present measurement is the first to be performed in the momentum range of interest for neutrino factory designs, and the first to provide the double-differential production cross-sections for charged pions emitted at large angles by protons on tantalum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of our experiment are in reasonable agreement with other experiments and with the predictions of several models.
we have measured the double-differential production cross-sections for positive and negative pions in the range of 100 MeV to 800 Mev and the angular range of 0.35 rad to 2.15 rad.
the results presented here are of particular importance for future neutrino factory design studies and that they provide an important reference data set for hadronic interaction models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pion yields in the momentum and angular range relevant to neutrino factory designs can be predicted with reasonable precision using existing Monte-Carlo generators.
the neutrino flux from a pion source is not proportional to the incident proton beam power.
pion production is dominated by the production of positive pions, and that the yields are very similar for positive and negative pions.
